reviewFindings: Authorization/side-effects: the `mountSurfaceRpc` child fiber is created UNCONDITIONALLY (both branches call `ctx.inject(['connection','webServer'], cb)` when `ctx.inject` exists, else `mountSurfaceRpc(ctx)`). In headless (no ctx.inject callback run) nothing is mounted — no route is exposed, no authority is granted; the surface only mounts when connection+webServer are present (web). Verified live: web 200 on the channel, headless never mounts it.

Packaging: the manifest change is the ONLY install gate that matters (app-boot `unmetRequirements`). Checked that `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a non-`dsh` peer and is skipped by the preflight (`name !== '@deepseek-ai/dsh' && !name.startsWith('@deepseek-ai/dsh-')` -> continue), so tightening it to `~4.0.5` (satisfied by the shipped cordis 4.0.5) cannot brake loading; it only aligns the declared family with dsh-base's own `~4.0.5`.

Compat scripts: verify-release.mjs was read in full — it does NOT hard-code any DSH version; it delegates to hostCompatFailures(root), which reads the matrix. So only the matrix + peer range + dshVersions needed to move. Confirmed by green verify-release after the change.

Transaction/compat risk from narrowing inject: dropping the static `connection` inject must not regress web. Verified live that the web profile still mounts the Native Control Surface (200 + plugin envelope) and that the connection-dependent code paths (ctx.connection.rpc.handle / webServer.register) all live inside src/control-surface/rpc.mjs, which is only ever called from the sub-fiber via mountSurfaceRpc. grep of src/ for `ctx.connection`/`webServer` found no other live consumer.

Docs: grep for `0.1.7` across README/PLUGINS/guide/architecture/AGENTS/HANDOFF returned nothing user-facing that still claims old-host support; remaining `0.1.7-*` strings are historical release records in docs/memory and .agents/workstreams, which I annotated (project-state.md/risks.md) rather than rewrote, to avoid falsifying history.

One accepted limitation: the plugin still declares `peerDependenciesMeta['@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'].optional=true`, but that meta does not exempt anything now — with `engines.dsh` present the peer is not evaluated at all. Kept for consumer-side npm install comfort; harmless.
